blind_spots.blind_spot: Wraith is a rendering while the DIU adoption clock is already running
blind_spots.operator_reality: DRM3 selection means an INDOPACOM unit expects hardware, training, spares, and a sustainment tail on Project G.I.'s timeline; the flagship platform is still shown as a 3D model, and months-to-field beyond the funded period is exactly where transitions die.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: A 2024-founded, move-fast El Segundo team optimizes for winning downselects; nothing in their language addresses who trains the unit, who fixes Wraith forward, or battery/spares logistics.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 3D visual prototype of Wraith in development

blind_spots.blind_spot: Vadris depends on an FPV video link inside the very spectrum fight it sells
blind_spots.operator_reality: Overlaying line-of-bearing 'onto the FPV video feed' assumes the video downlink survives; in the contested EMS they describe, adversary jamming and their own emissions-control rules degrade that link first — the operator loses the overlay exactly when hunting the emitter matters.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The seeker is the product; the fragile COTS FPV control/video link is treated as a given because demos happen on clean ranges.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: overlaying their direction onto the FPV video feed. This enables the operator to follow a real-time line of bearing toward the signal's source

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Open by Design' integration with tactical networks that never names TAK or an accreditation path
blind_spots.operator_reality: Emitter coordinates reach a fires cell or ground force through ATAK/TAK and accredited C2 systems; in ~1,200 words touching situational awareness and 'C2 tools, and tactical networks' there is no ATAK, no ATO/RMF, no ITAR language — the government back-end integration that turns a downselect into fielded kit is unstated.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: RF and platform engineers (SpaceX/Raytheon lineage) build the emitter chain; the accreditation and TAK plumbing feels like paperwork until it gates the INDOPACOM deployment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: seamlessly integrate with your existing sensors, C2 tools, and tactical networks. No lock-in, just combat-ready interoperability.

opener_hook: CX2's April DRM3 dual-selection puts Wraith on an INDOPACOM adoption clock while the company's own site still labels it a '3D visual prototype in development.'
what_they_do: AI-enabled electronic-warfare hardware/software — an RF-seeking FPV payload (Vadris) and an autonomous airborne EW drone (Wraith) — to find and target enemy emitters.
